paragraphs.title: Joshua grows old and calls the leaders

easy.question: Who gave rest to Israel according to the first verse?
answers: The LORD
Joshua
Their enemies
easy.explanation: The verse says 'the Lord had given rest unto Israel' — the LORD granted them rest.

easy.question: What does the verse indicate about Joshua's condition?
answers: That he was old
That he was young
That he was strong
easy.explanation: 'Joshua waxed old and stricken in age' shows he was advanced in years.

easy.question: Whom did Joshua call in verse 2?
answers: All the people
Only his family
His elders, chiefs, judges, and officers
easy.explanation: The verse lists elders, heads, judges, and officers as those he summoned.

medium.question: What is the likely reason Joshua called the elders and leaders according to the verses?
answers: To speak to them in his old age and final days
To celebrate with the people
To invite the enemies
medium.explanation: Given that he was elderly and the land was at rest, it's natural he called leaders to give final instructions.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'had given rest' imply in the context 'the Lord had given rest unto Israel'?
answers: He stopped the wars and granted rest
He utterly destroyed them
He made them slaves
medium.explanation: Here 'given rest' means the LORD removed or subdued their enemies and granted Israel rest from hostilities.

medium.question: Which group is not mentioned in the list Joshua called?
answers: Elders
Judges
Prophets
medium.explanation: The verse mentions elders, heads, judges, and officers — prophets are not listed.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'a long time after' suggest about the time that passed?
answers: A short period
A few weeks
A long period
challenge.explanation: 'A long time after' indicates a lengthy period, not a brief one.

challenge.question: The list (elders, heads, judges, officers) mainly indicates what kind of leadership or organization in Israel at that time?
answers: Tribal/local leadership with elders and judges
A strong centralized monarchy
A modern electoral system
challenge.explanation: Elders and judges point to tribal/local leadership and judicial authority rather than a centralized monarchy.

challenge.question: What does the English phrase 'waxed old and stricken in age' mean regarding Joshua?
answers: That he climbed a hill
That he was advanced in years/very old
That he traveled for many days
challenge.explanation: 'Waxed old and stricken in age' is an idiom meaning he grew very old.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'a long time after' suggest about the time that passed?
answers: A short period
A few weeks
A long period
questions.explanation: 'A long time after' indicates a lengthy period, not a brief one.

questions.question: The list (elders, heads, judges, officers) mainly indicates what kind of leadership or organization in Israel at that time?
answers: Tribal/local leadership with elders and judges
A strong centralized monarchy
A modern electoral system
questions.explanation: Elders and judges point to tribal/local leadership and judicial authority rather than a centralized monarchy.

questions.question: What does the English phrase 'waxed old and stricken in age' mean regarding Joshua?
answers: That he climbed a hill
That he was advanced in years/very old
That he traveled for many days
questions.explanation: 'Waxed old and stricken in age' is an idiom meaning he grew very old.

paragraphs.title: Recalling the Lord's deeds and the inheritances

easy.question: Who fought for Israel according to the verse?
answers: The LORD their God
Joshua
The local peoples
easy.explanation: The verse states 'for the Lord your God he it is that hath fought for you' — God fought for them.

easy.question: What had the Israelites seen, as stated in the verse?
answers: The cloud's movement in the wilderness
All that the Lord your God had done to these nations before you
Only the parting of the sea
easy.explanation: The verse says they saw 'all that the Lord your God hath done unto all these nations' — God's acts against the nations.

easy.question: What did the Israelites inherit according to the verses?
answers: Great wealth and silver
Only certain cities
The land of those nations
easy.explanation: The passage speaks of inheriting the lands of the nations the LORD dispossessed.

medium.question: What does 'hath fought for you' mean in the phrase 'for the Lord your God he it is that hath fought for you'?
answers: A person celebrating with song
The one who fought on your behalf
The judge who punishes
medium.explanation: 'Hath fought for you' means the LORD fought on behalf of Israel against their foes.

medium.question: According to the verses, why was the inheritance given to the tribes?
answers: Because the LORD fought and dispossessed the nations before you
Because the Israelites first fought themselves
Because the nations voluntarily yielded
medium.explanation: The text attributes the dispossession of the nations to the LORD, making the land the LORD's gift.

medium.question: The inheritance is from the Jordan to which boundary according to the verse?
answers: To another eastern river
To the Red Sea
To the great sea westward (the Mediterranean)
medium.explanation: The phrase 'the great sea westward' refers to the sea on the west — the Mediterranean Sea.

challenge.question: Which sea is called 'the great sea westward'?
answers: The Dead Sea
The Mediterranean Sea
The Red Sea
challenge.explanation: 'Westward' points to the sea on the west of the land, i.e., the Mediterranean.

challenge.question: How does the verse guarantee that the land will be given to Israel?
answers: As the LORD had spoken — a divine promise fulfilled
By treaties with distant kingdoms
Subject to a special tax they must pay
challenge.explanation: The verse says the land will be given 'as the Lord your God hath promised unto you' — a divine promise.

challenge.question: According to the verses, who drives out the nations and who inherits their land?
answers: The Israelites drive them out and the LORD inherits the land
The LORD will drive them out before you and you shall inherit their land
The nations will give the land to the priests only
challenge.explanation: The passage states the LORD will drive out the nations and Israel shall possess their land.

questions.question: Which sea is called 'the great sea westward'?
answers: The Dead Sea
The Mediterranean Sea
The Red Sea
questions.explanation: 'Westward' points to the sea on the west of the land, i.e., the Mediterranean.

questions.question: How does the verse guarantee that the land will be given to Israel?
answers: As the LORD had spoken — a divine promise fulfilled
By treaties with distant kingdoms
Subject to a special tax they must pay
questions.explanation: The verse says the land will be given 'as the Lord your God hath promised unto you' — a divine promise.

questions.question: According to the verses, who drives out the nations and who inherits their land?
answers: The Israelites drive them out and the LORD inherits the land
The LORD will drive them out before you and you shall inherit their land
The nations will give the land to the priests only
questions.explanation: The passage states the LORD will drive out the nations and Israel shall possess their land.

easy.question: What does the verse command them to do?
answers: Be strong to keep and do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses
Leave the books alone
Emigrate to another land
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to be very courageous to keep and do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses.

easy.question: Which book is referred to in the verse?
answers: The book of Joshua
The book of the law of Moses
The book of Chronicles
easy.explanation: The text explicitly mentions 'the book of the law of Moses'.

easy.question: What does 'that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left' mean?
answers: To follow it only when righteous
To adhere to the rules without deviating from them
To practice walking right and left only
easy.explanation: The phrase means not to deviate from the law — not to turn aside to either side.

medium.question: Why is 'Be ye therefore very courageous' said before the command to keep and do the written law?
answers: Because they needed physical strength for building
Because there was no need to act now
To emphasize determination to keep the law
medium.explanation: 'Very' adds emphasis — it stresses determination and resolve to obey the law.

medium.question: What does 'turn aside' mean in this context 'that ye turn not aside'?
answers: To depart or deviate from the law
To write something in the book
To strengthen someone
medium.explanation: Here 'turn aside' means to deviate or depart from the commandments of the law.

medium.question: Why does the verse stress 'to the right hand or to the left'?
answers: To indicate only physical directions
To emphasize not deviating from the law in any direction
Because it refers to right- and left-seafaring
medium.explanation: The expression emphasizes that they must not stray in any direction — full obedience is required.

challenge.question: To whom is the command 'Be ye therefore very courageous' addressed?
answers: The governments of neighboring nations
The people of Israel
Only the priests
challenge.explanation: Joshua addresses all the Israelites, charging them to keep the law.

challenge.question: What does the addition 'very' in 'Be ye therefore very courageous' express?
answers: That only physical strength is required
That it praises past compliance
Urgency and intensity of commitment
challenge.explanation: 'Very' heightens the command, conveying urgency and strong commitment.

challenge.question: What historical-cultural threat likely prompted Joshua's warning not to turn right or left?
answers: To avoid the influence of neighboring idol worship
To avoid trade with neighboring peoples
So they would not get lost in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: A main threat was religious influence from surrounding peoples, leading to idolatry and syncretism.

questions.question: To whom is the command 'Be ye therefore very courageous' addressed?
answers: The governments of neighboring nations
The people of Israel
Only the priests
questions.explanation: Joshua addresses all the Israelites, charging them to keep the law.

questions.question: What does the addition 'very' in 'Be ye therefore very courageous' express?
answers: That only physical strength is required
That it praises past compliance
Urgency and intensity of commitment
questions.explanation: 'Very' heightens the command, conveying urgency and strong commitment.

questions.question: What historical-cultural threat likely prompted Joshua's warning not to turn right or left?
answers: To avoid the influence of neighboring idol worship
To avoid trade with neighboring peoples
So they would not get lost in the wilderness
questions.explanation: A main threat was religious influence from surrounding peoples, leading to idolatry and syncretism.

paragraphs.title: Prohibition of intermingling with the nations

easy.question: What is forbidden in verse 7 regarding 'the name of their gods'?
answers: To mention their names
To write their names in the Bible
To teach their language
easy.explanation: The verse forbids making mention of the names of the nations' gods.

easy.question: Which action is expressly forbidden in verse 7?
answers: Marrying foreigners
To swear by their gods
To trade with them
easy.explanation: The verse includes 'neither cause to swear by them' — swearing by their gods is forbidden.

easy.question: What does verse 8 command them to do instead of serving the nations' gods?
answers: To strengthen the army
To cleave unto the Lord your God
To migrate to another land
easy.explanation: Verse 8 directs them to 'cleave unto the Lord your God' — to cling to and be faithful to the LORD.

medium.question: Why does the verse forbid mentioning and swearing by the nations' gods?
answers: To prevent military conflicts
To preserve faithfulness to the covenant with the LORD
Because their gods' names are unimportant
medium.explanation: The prohibition aims to keep Israel faithful to the covenant with the LORD and prevent religious contamination.

medium.question: What does 'cleave' mean in the phrase 'But cleave unto the Lord your God'?
answers: To separate from them
To cling and be faithful
To build walls between you
medium.explanation: 'Cleave' here means to cling to or remain faithful and devoted to the LORD.

medium.question: In verse 8 it says 'as ye have done unto this day' — what does this mean?
answers: That you should continue in the practices you have done up to now
That you should begin new practices
That you should forget the past
medium.explanation: The phrase urges them to continue in the loyalty they have shown up to that point.

challenge.question: What is a practical reason for forbidding mention of the nations' gods?
answers: To prevent breaking political treaties
To prevent making oaths or contracts by their gods
Because their names were hard to pronounce
challenge.explanation: Avoiding mention prevents taking vows or making legal commitments invoking foreign gods, which could compromise loyalty to the LORD.

challenge.question: What is the distinct difference between 'you shall not serve them' and 'you shall not bow yourselves unto them' in verse 7?
answers: Two identical expressions with no difference
'Serve' emphasizes ritual service, 'bow' emphasizes physical prostration and recognition as gods
One refers to trade and the other to marriage
challenge.explanation: 'Serve' speaks of ritual service and worship, while 'bow' emphasizes physical prostration and acknowledgment of deity.

challenge.question: What historical-cultural danger are these verses trying to prevent among Israel?
answers: Military conquest by neighboring peoples
Religious syncretism and breach of the covenant due to foreign cultic influences
Agricultural problems because of idol worship
challenge.explanation: The aim is to prevent syncretism — adopting foreign cultic practices that would violate the covenant with God.

questions.question: What is a practical reason for forbidding mention of the nations' gods?
answers: To prevent breaking political treaties
To prevent making oaths or contracts by their gods
Because their names were hard to pronounce
questions.explanation: Avoiding mention prevents taking vows or making legal commitments invoking foreign gods, which could compromise loyalty to the LORD.

questions.question: What is the distinct difference between 'you shall not serve them' and 'you shall not bow yourselves unto them' in verse 7?
answers: Two identical expressions with no difference
'Serve' emphasizes ritual service, 'bow' emphasizes physical prostration and recognition as gods
One refers to trade and the other to marriage
questions.explanation: 'Serve' speaks of ritual service and worship, while 'bow' emphasizes physical prostration and acknowledgment of deity.

questions.question: What historical-cultural danger are these verses trying to prevent among Israel?
answers: Military conquest by neighboring peoples
Religious syncretism and breach of the covenant due to foreign cultic influences
Agricultural problems because of idol worship
questions.explanation: The aim is to prevent syncretism — adopting foreign cultic practices that would violate the covenant with God.

paragraphs.title: Remembrance of victories and love for the LORD

easy.question: What did the LORD do for the people according to verse 9?
answers: He dispossessed great and strong nations before them
He gave them abundant food
He belittled their abilities
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says the LORD drove out great and strong nations before Israel.

easy.question: What does 'One of you shall chase a thousand' literally mean in verse 10?
answers: One will flee before a thousand
One of you shall chase a thousand
Each of you shall chase only ten
easy.explanation: The expression means that one person will be able to pursue a thousand, indicating great success in battle.

easy.question: What does verse 11 command the people to do toward the LORD?
answers: Build many temples
Love the LORD your God
Fast all year
easy.explanation: Verse 11 explicitly commands them to love the LORD their God.

medium.question: How do verses 9–10 explain the cause of Israel's victories?
answers: Because of advanced military tactics
Because the LORD dispossessed the nations and fought for them
Because neighboring states joined them
medium.explanation: The text attributes victories to the LORD driving out nations and fighting for Israel.

medium.question: What does 'take good heed unto yourselves' imply in the command to love the LORD your God?
answers: To guard your lives and spiritual well-being
To guard wealth and possessions
To simply remember customs
medium.explanation: The warning to 'take good heed' means to protect both life and moral/spiritual wellbeing in order to love God faithfully.

medium.question: Why is 'take good heed' emphasized before the command to love the LORD?
answers: Because love of the LORD requires care and active effort
Because the LORD did not forgive in the past
Because they needed lots of gold
medium.explanation: The emphasis indicates that loving the LORD requires vigilance, effort, and moral care.

challenge.question: What rhetorical effect does the phrase 'one of you shall chase a thousand' have?
answers: It describes mere technical military ability
It promises that only one hero will appear each generation
It is hyperbolic to show that God's help makes one effective against many
challenge.explanation: The phrase is rhetorical exaggeration emphasizing that God's aid enables a few to overcome many.

challenge.question: What does the term 'dispossessed' (v.9 'the Lord hath driven out') suggest about how Israel received the land?
answers: That the LORD removed and gave the nations' land to Israel
That they bought the land in trade
That the local peoples remained in control
challenge.explanation: 'Driven out' indicates God removed the prior inhabitants and handed the land to Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from linking God's fighting for the people with the command 'that ye love the Lord your God'?
answers: That the priesthood alone was responsible for victories
That victories are the result of the covenant with God and obligate love and faithfulness
That victories caused the people to become proud and abandon the Law
challenge.explanation: Since God fought for them, the text implies a covenant obligation of gratitude expressed as love and faithfulness.

questions.question: What rhetorical effect does the phrase 'one of you shall chase a thousand' have?
answers: It describes mere technical military ability
It promises that only one hero will appear each generation
It is hyperbolic to show that God's help makes one effective against many
questions.explanation: The phrase is rhetorical exaggeration emphasizing that God's aid enables a few to overcome many.

questions.question: What does the term 'dispossessed' (v.9 'the Lord hath driven out') suggest about how Israel received the land?
answers: That the LORD removed and gave the nations' land to Israel
That they bought the land in trade
That the local peoples remained in control
questions.explanation: 'Driven out' indicates God removed the prior inhabitants and handed the land to Israel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from linking God's fighting for the people with the command 'that ye love the Lord your God'?
answers: That the priesthood alone was responsible for victories
That victories are the result of the covenant with God and obligate love and faithfulness
That victories caused the people to become proud and abandon the Law
questions.explanation: Since God fought for them, the text implies a covenant obligation of gratitude expressed as love and faithfulness.

easy.question: What action does the verse warn them not to do?
answers: Return and cleave to the remaining nations
Go to war against them
Build altars for them as part of a new covenant
easy.explanation: Verse 12 warns against going back and cleaving to the remnant of the nations among them.

easy.question: What might happen if Israel 'go in unto them, and they to you' as the verse says?
answers: Israel will expel the nations completely
Israel will be assimilated and influenced by them
Israel will immediately gain great blessing without risk
easy.explanation: The text warns that intermingling will lead to Israel being influenced and assimilated by foreign practices.

easy.question: According to verse 13, who will 'no more drive out' these nations from before you?
answers: The local leaders
The people themselves
The LORD your God
easy.explanation: Verse 13 states that the LORD your God will no longer drive out those nations if you cleave to them.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'and they shall be snares and traps unto you' emphasize?
answers: That the situation is one of complete victory over the nations
That both sides will influence each other and become entangled
That the nations will flee without trace
medium.explanation: The phrase warns of entanglement — the nations will become snares and traps leading Israel into danger.

medium.question: What does 'snare' mean in 'snares and traps'?
answers: A trap or danger that will ensnare you
A holy place for spiritual restoration
A symbol of military victory
medium.explanation: Here 'snare' denotes a trap or hazard that leads to harm or downfall.

medium.question: What long-term result does the verse warn will occur if this happens?
answers: The people will grow stronger and expand their borders
The people will remain free but lose a little wealth
The people will perish from off the good land
medium.explanation: The verse warns that such assimilation will lead to their perishing from off the good land.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'and thorns in your eyes' likely describe in context?
answers: A lasting feeling of fear or shame before your eyes
Beautiful objects that will be seen by the people with joy
Economic prosperity visible to all
challenge.explanation: In the context of calamities and hazards, 'thorns in your eyes' suggests ongoing pain, shame, or distress seen by all.

challenge.question: What does 'from before you' in 'the Lord will no more drive out any of these nations from before you' imply about what had happened earlier?
answers: That until now the LORD had already driven out some nations from before Israel
That they had never tried to drive out the nations
That the nations arrived only after Israel had conquered the land
challenge.explanation: 'From before you' implies that previously the LORD had driven out nations ahead of Israel, but He will cease to do so if they assimilate.

challenge.question: What added severity appears in verse 13 compared to verse 12?
answers: The verse adds that the nations will become actual snares and dangers for you
The verse promises that foreign help will arrive
The verse promises Israel will receive greater wealth
challenge.explanation: Verse 13 intensifies the warning: the nations will become snares, scourges, and thorns until Israel perishes from the land.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'and thorns in your eyes' likely describe in context?
answers: A lasting feeling of fear or shame before your eyes
Beautiful objects that will be seen by the people with joy
Economic prosperity visible to all
questions.explanation: In the context of calamities and hazards, 'thorns in your eyes' suggests ongoing pain, shame, or distress seen by all.

questions.question: What does 'from before you' in 'the Lord will no more drive out any of these nations from before you' imply about what had happened earlier?
answers: That until now the LORD had already driven out some nations from before Israel
That they had never tried to drive out the nations
That the nations arrived only after Israel had conquered the land
questions.explanation: 'From before you' implies that previously the LORD had driven out nations ahead of Israel, but He will cease to do so if they assimilate.

questions.question: What added severity appears in verse 13 compared to verse 12?
answers: The verse adds that the nations will become actual snares and dangers for you
The verse promises that foreign help will arrive
The verse promises Israel will receive greater wealth
questions.explanation: Verse 13 intensifies the warning: the nations will become snares, scourges, and thorns until Israel perishes from the land.

paragraphs.title: Testimony of fulfillment and warning of punishment

easy.question: What is said about the good things the LORD promised the people?
answers: All the good things have come to pass; not one failed
Only some of the good things were fulfilled
The good things did not occur
easy.explanation: The verse affirms that not one of the good things promised by the LORD failed to come to pass.

easy.question: What will happen if the people act contrary to the word of the LORD?
answers: The LORD will bring evil upon them until He destroys them from off the land
The LORD will withdraw blessings but keep them in the land
The LORD will send additional prophets only
easy.explanation: The passage warns that if they disobey, the LORD will bring evils until He destroys them from the good land.

easy.question: To what does the phrase 'this good land' refer?
answers: The land the LORD gave them as a gift
The land of neighboring nations only
A single city
easy.explanation: 'This good land' refers to the land the LORD gave to Israel.

medium.question: Why does Joshua say 'behold, I am going the way of all the earth' before saying that nothing failed?
answers: To show he has traveled the land and can testify the promises were fulfilled
To announce he immediately leaves the people
To describe an upcoming conquest
medium.explanation: Joshua notes his impending death and his knowledge of the land to testify that God's promises were fulfilled.

medium.question: What does 'failed' mean in the phrase 'not one thing hath failed'?
answers: Not come to pass / failed to be realized
Physically fallen
Occurred noticeably
medium.explanation: Here 'failed' means 'failed to occur' — nothing promised failed to be realized.

medium.question: How does the verse link God's past deeds to future punishment?
answers: It shows that as God fulfilled promises of good, so He can bring evil things as judgment for disobedience
It says past blessings guarantee no future punishments
It separates past promises and future punishments without relation
medium.explanation: The text presents God's faithfulness in delivering good as grounds for His ability to bring judgment if Israel disobeys.

challenge.question: What is the main purpose of the warning 'until he have destroyed you from off the good land' in the covenant context?
answers: To warn of destruction and exile as punishment for violating the covenant
To recount an event that already happened
To announce that the land will remain forever regardless of people's actions
challenge.explanation: The warning serves to show the severe consequence (destruction/exile) of breaking the covenant.

challenge.question: What can be inferred about Israel's faith from the phrase 'not one thing hath failed of all the good things'?
answers: Their faith in God's faithfulness is strengthened — they saw promises fulfilled
They were skeptical about God's word, and the phrase expresses hope only
They had no special regard for fulfillment of promises
challenge.explanation: The fulfillment of promises would reinforce their trust in God's faithfulness.

challenge.question: In 'so shall the Lord bring upon you all evil things' — who is the source and what does it mean?
answers: The LORD is the source who brings both good and evil as consequence of actions
Joshua will bring punishment by means of the army
Neighboring nations will bring evil as revenge
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says the LORD will be the agent of both blessing and punishment according to their behavior.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the warning 'until he have destroyed you from off the good land' in the covenant context?
answers: To warn of destruction and exile as punishment for violating the covenant
To recount an event that already happened
To announce that the land will remain forever regardless of people's actions
questions.explanation: The warning serves to show the severe consequence (destruction/exile) of breaking the covenant.

questions.question: What can be inferred about Israel's faith from the phrase 'not one thing hath failed of all the good things'?
answers: Their faith in God's faithfulness is strengthened — they saw promises fulfilled
They were skeptical about God's word, and the phrase expresses hope only
They had no special regard for fulfillment of promises
questions.explanation: The fulfillment of promises would reinforce their trust in God's faithfulness.

questions.question: In 'so shall the Lord bring upon you all evil things' — who is the source and what does it mean?
answers: The LORD is the source who brings both good and evil as consequence of actions
Joshua will bring punishment by means of the army
Neighboring nations will bring evil as revenge
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says the LORD will be the agent of both blessing and punishment according to their behavior.

easy.question: What will happen if the people transgress the covenant and bow to other gods?
answers: The anger of the LORD will be kindled and they shall quickly perish from off the good land
They will receive an additional blessing
They will become stronger against their enemies
easy.explanation: The verse warns that if they serve other gods the LORD's anger will come and they will perish from the land.

easy.question: Who expresses anger in the verse?
answers: The land
The LORD
The neighbors
easy.explanation: The text says 'the anger of the Lord' — the anger is God's.

easy.question: To which land does the verse finally refer?
answers: The land of Egypt
The wilderness
The good land
easy.explanation: The verse refers to 'the good land' which the LORD had given them.

medium.question: What is the connection between covenant violation and serving other gods in the result described?
answers: Violation brings the LORD's anger and their destruction
The covenant guarantees them protection even if they sin
Violation will result in receiving additional lands
medium.explanation: The passage links disobedience (serving other gods) directly to divine anger and removal from the land.

medium.question: What does 'kindled' mean in 'the anger of the Lord be kindled'?
answers: Physical heating
Great anger
Great joy
medium.explanation: Here 'kindled' describes intense or burning anger.

medium.question: What exactly is forbidden to avoid the described punishment?
answers: To leave the land
To go and serve other gods and bow to them
To participate in local festivals without belief
medium.explanation: The verse forbids walking and serving other gods and bowing to them — that conduct brings punishment.

challenge.question: What does 'from off the land' in 'ye shall perish quickly from off the good land' convey?
answers: That they will remain in the land under partial punishment
That the punishment means they will be removed entirely from the land (exile/destruction)
That they will live in the land with reduced status
challenge.explanation: 'Perish from off the land' implies removal from the land — exile or destruction, not mere reduced status.

challenge.question: What can be inferred about the relation between keeping the covenant and remaining in the good land?
answers: Keeping the covenant is connected to continued residence in the good land
There is no relation between covenant and staying in the land
The covenant is only symbolic and has no practical effect
challenge.explanation: The verse links obedience to the covenant with continued possession of the good land.

challenge.question: According to the verse, who gave them the good land?
answers: God gave you the good land
The king conquered and granted it
The people bought the land by force and money
challenge.explanation: The verse states the good land was given to them (by the LORD).
